description:
I’m Wahaj, a pre-medical student. I’ve worked on machine learning, medical imaging, computer vision, and app development.

For NASA Space Apps, I’m building a team to explore NASA datasets and create something meaningful. You don’t need to be an expert, just curious, willing to learn, contribute, and collaborate.
summary:
ORION is a self-assessment app that lets astronauts log their own health readings and emotion checks during long missions. Each reading is compared against calibrated ranges, and a digital body map shows which systems need attention. Each guidance card links to a NASA Human Research Program hazard, such as radiation or isolation, so the app explains why each measurement matters. Emotion checks accept text, photos, or voice, and photos are analysed in the browser and never uploaded. The app works offline and syncs when the connection returns.

It addresses the challenge by giving crews a way to track their own health and mood without waiting for ground support. This matters because long missions are isolated, and small changes in health or mood can become serious if they go unnoticed. ORION is a student demo, not clinical software, but it shows how this kind of monitoring could work.
details:
ORION is a self-assessment tool for astronauts on long missions. Astronauts log their own readings, including blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, blood sugar, sleep, emotion checks, exercise, and bone scans. Each reading is compared against a stable range set during calibration(assigned by us through NASA datasets ), and values outside it show as critical. A digital twin of the body colors each area by its latest status, and each guidance card links to the matching NASA Human Research Program hazard, such as radiation or isolation.

The emotion check works three ways. Text is matched against emotion words. Photos are analysed by a face-expression model that runs in the browser, so images are never uploaded. Voice uses a rough acoustic heuristic based on loudness, pitch, and pace.

The frontend uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with hand-built SVG charts. The backend uses FastAPI and SQLite, and the project is deployed on Render. Readings save offline and sync when the connection returns.

ORION is a demo for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, not clinical software. Its goal is to show how a crew could track their own health and mood, and how those readings connect to known spaceflight hazards. A real version would need proper authentication, validated ranges, and review by mission medical teams.
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
